discovery: Topological (surface-code) quantum error correction and its fault-tolerance threshold

nominees.name: Sergey Bravyi
nominees.affiliation: IBM Quantum, Thomas J. Watson Research Center, USA

subfield: Quantum information physics / quantum error correction
motivation: Kitaev's toric code (1997), the planar surface code of Bravyi and Kitaev (1998), and the statistical-mechanics threshold analysis of Dennis, Kitaev, Landahl and Preskill (2002) showed that quantum information can be stored nonlocally in a topologically ordered many-body state. Local errors can then be corrected with only nearest-neighbour measurements, and a high error threshold of about 1% follows. This insight turned the fragility of quantum coherence from a seemingly fundamental barrier into a quantitative engineering target. It set the error budgets that experimentalists have worked to meet for two decades. In 2024–25 superconducting processors showed logical error rates falling exponentially with code distance, operating below threshold. This confirmed that the physics predicted by these theories holds in real devices. The work connects topological phases of matter with the practical route to scalable quantum computation, and it now shapes the architecture of every major hardware platform.
